pageTitle: Klacks for Hotels & Restaurants in Switzerland | Rosters with L-GAV Checks

hero.titleHtml: Early, late, night shift — L-GAV rules in view.
hero.subtitle: Klacks plans service, kitchen and housekeeping under the Swiss Employment Act and the L-GAV — the collective labour agreement that is generally binding for all hospitality businesses, with a 42-hour target working week, two rest days per week and the 7-day rule.
hero.screenshotAlt: Klacks timeline view for rosters in hotels and restaurants in Switzerland

items.title: The L-GAV applies to everyone
items.text: The L-GAV has been declared generally binding by the Federal Council — it applies to every hospitality business, member or not. 42 target working hours (seasonal businesses 43.5, small businesses 45) instead of the statutory 50 are not a voluntary bonus but an obligation.

items.title: 7 days in a row — but done right
items.text: The L-GAV allows up to seven working days in a row — but only with a maximum of 9 hours of daily working time followed by at least 83 hours off. On top of that come two rest days per week. Chaining this together by hand is error-prone.

items.title: Nights & few Sundays off
items.text: Night and Sunday work in hospitality requires no permit, and Sundays off can be reduced to four per year — in return, the night premiums (+25 % for temporary, +10 % time for regular night work) must be shown properly.

solutions.title: How Klacks takes the load off hotels & restaurants
solutions.subtitle: From the early shift to the night shift — everything works together.

items.title: L-GAV stored as a rule set
items.text: 42-hour target, two rest days per week, 7-day sequence with 83 hours of compensation — you store the L-GAV requirements as a rule set, and Klacks makes every breach of them visible immediately.

items.title: Rest periods in view
items.text: Eleven hours of rest under Art. 15a ArG — can be shortened to 8 hours at most once a week, provided the average over two weeks stays at 11 hours. Klacks checks the stored rest-period limits in real time and warns of breaches.

items.title: 14-hour span respected
items.text: Day and evening work including breaks must fit within the 14-hour span, and night work is limited to 9 to 10 hours — Klacks checks the maximum daily working times you store and warns before they are exceeded; you keep an eye on the 14-hour span including breaks yourself.

items.title: Night premiums as time credit
items.text: +25 % pay for temporary, +10 % time for regular night work (11pm to 6am) — Klacks credits the stored time premium as time credit and provides the hours for payroll; Klacks does not calculate the pay premium.

items.title: Klacksy understands your request
items.text: “Plan the weekend, two service staff are off sick” is all it takes — Klacksy starts the replanning.

items.title: Absences covered quickly
items.text: If someone drops out, Klacks immediately shows who is qualified, available and within the rest-period and maximum-working-time limits.
